newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold steady, silver stable after recent fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold steady, silver stable after recent fall.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 5 rupees higher at 4,780 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,775 rupees on the back of fresh seasonal buying and restricted inflow. Gold was up by 25 rupees on Saturday.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed steady at 55,900 rupees per piece after gaining 300 rupees on Saturday. They were up by 1,100 rupees per piece during last week.

** Silver (.999) closed steady at 7,040 rupees per kg after opening 5 rupees higher at 7,045 rupees against the previous close of 7,040 rupees amid limited activity. Silver was up by 10 rupees per kg on Saturday but was down by 285 rupees last week.

Gold 24 carat closed 5 rupees higher at 4,780 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,775 rupees on the back of fresh seasonal buying for the approaching wedding season while offerings were limited amid restricted arrivals, dealers said.
Gold was up by 25 rupees per 10 gramme on Saturday.
"Arrivals remained low due to thin imports and absence of fresh offerings by the customs department," they said.
Confiscated smuggled gold is sold periodically by the customs department, but sales have been curtailed due to low stocks.

Prices of gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed steady at 55,900 rupees per piece amid limited activity during the day after a rise of 300 rupees per piece recorded on Saturday. Biscuits were up by 1,100 rupees per piece during last week.
Trading remained limited today but sentiment at the close was firm on expectation of higher seasonal buying in the coming days.

Silver (.999) on the other hand closed steady at 7,040 rupees per kg after opening 5 rupees higher at 7,045 rupees against the previous close of 7,040 rupees as sluggish industrial buying trimmed early gains towards the close. Fresh arrivals also remained low today, one broker said. Silver was up by 10 rupees per kg on Saturday but was down by 285 rupees last week.
"Bombay Bullion market will remain closed on Tuesday for a Hindu festival and will reopen for trading on Wednesday," dealer said.
